variables.label: Start-year intercept a_t
steps: One intercept per start year, fit by the model. It absorbs anything that moved every neighborhood that year.
A start year the model has not seen gets the average of the intercepts it has seen.
It shifts every neighborhood equally, so it never changes the ranking.

variables.label: Starting price vs the city
variables.fields: sale price ÷ residential units, 1–3 family homes
steps: Median price per unit of 1–3 family sales ≥ $10,000 in years t−3 and t−2.
Divide by the same median for the whole city, then take the log (×100).
0 = priced like the city; +50 ≈ 65% above it.

variables.label: Median household income
steps: Each tract's median household income from the 5-year release ending t−2.
NTA value = household-weighted average of its tracts' medians.
Natural log.

variables.label: Median gross rent
steps: Each tract's median gross rent, release ending t−2.
NTA value = renter-household-weighted average.
Natural log.

variables.label: College share
steps: Adults 25+ with a bachelor's or higher ÷ all adults 25+, summed over the NTA's tracts. Percent.

variables.label: Renter share
steps: Renter households ÷ all households, summed over the NTA's tracts. Percent.

variables.label: Own momentum (3-yr price change vs city)
steps: log(P[t−2] ÷ P[t−5]) minus the same for the city, ×100.
P[t−2] uses sales in t−3 and t−2; P[t−5] uses t−6 and t−5. No sale is shared with the outcome.

variables.label: Construction activity (new buildings + demolitions)
variables.fields: BIS NB + DM jobs; DOB NOW New Building + Full Demolition
steps: Count new-building and full-demolition jobs by the year their first permit was issued (BIS and DOB NOW combined).
Average of t−3 and t−2, per 1,000 households, then log(1 + rate).

variables.label: New-building permits
variables.fields: BIS NB; DOB NOW New Building
steps: Same as construction activity, new buildings only.

variables.label: Demolition permits
variables.fields: BIS DM; DOB NOW Full Demolition
steps: Same as construction activity, demolitions only.

variables.label: Renovation permits
variables.fields: BIS A1; DOB NOW Alteration CO
steps: Major alterations that change use or occupancy. Per 1,000 households, log(1 + rate).

variables.label: Home sales volume
steps: Count residential sales (all types), average of t−3 and t−2, per 1,000 households, log(1 + rate).

variables.label: Felony rate vs the city
steps: Felonies placed in the NTA by coordinates, t−3 and t−2.
log((felonies + 1) ÷ (what the city rate would give this many residents + 1)). 0 = the city rate.

variables.label: Felony change vs the city
steps: Felony rate in t−3…t−2 vs t−6…t−5 (non-overlapping), as a log ratio, minus the city's own change.

variables.label: Noise: residential / party
steps: 311 complaints of this kind placed in the NTA by coordinates, t−3 and t−2.
log((complaints + 1) ÷ (city rate × residents + 1)): 0 = the city rate, +0.69 = 2× the city.
Complaints, not decibels: they measure how often residents call, not how loud it is.

variables.label: Noise: bars, clubs, music (commercial)
steps: 311 complaints of this kind placed in the NTA by coordinates, t−3 and t−2.
log((complaints + 1) ÷ (city rate × residents + 1)): 0 = the city rate, +0.69 = 2× the city.
Complaints, not decibels: they measure how often residents call, not how loud it is.

variables.label: Noise: street / sidewalk
steps: 311 complaints of this kind placed in the NTA by coordinates, t−3 and t−2.
log((complaints + 1) ÷ (city rate × residents + 1)): 0 = the city rate, +0.69 = 2× the city.
Complaints, not decibels: they measure how often residents call, not how loud it is.

variables.label: Noise: construction (after-hours, jackhammering)
variables.fields: complaint_type = 'Noise' and (descriptor like '%Construction%' or descriptor like '%Jack Hammer%')
steps: 311 complaints of this kind placed in the NTA by coordinates, t−3 and t−2.
log((complaints + 1) ÷ (city rate × residents + 1)): 0 = the city rate, +0.69 = 2× the city.
Complaints, not decibels: they measure how often residents call, not how loud it is.

variables.label: Noise: all four kinds combined
steps: Same steps on the total. Used only to test split vs combined.

variables.label: Distance to the subway
steps: Each tract's center to the nearest station, km; NTA = population-weighted average. Fixed over time.

variables.label: Neighbors' momentum (average)
steps: Neighbors = NTAs sharing a border or corner (queen contiguity). Islands get their nearest NTA.
Average MOM over neighbors that pass the minimum-sales rule.

variables.label: Gap: hottest neighbor minus this one
steps: Take the highest MOM among qualifying neighbors and subtract this NTA's own MOM.
Large Gap = the area next door is surging and this one hasn't yet (the edge of a hot area).

variables.label: Place effect u_i
steps: One number per NTA: how much faster (or slower) its prices beat the city than its inputs say.
A Leroux CAR prior (a proper ICAR) pulls each u toward its neighbors' average AND toward 0; τ and the mix ρ are picked on the validation years.
A correction for what isn't measured but is shared locally; the Gap is how the model sees a hot side.
